'''Maurice Williams''' (born December 19, 1982) is an assistant men's [[basketball]] coach at the [[University of Kentucky]] and a former professional [[basketball]] player who played 13 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). After a successful high school career at [[Murrah High School]] in [[Jackson, Mississippi]], Williams attended college at the [[University of Alabama]], where he led his team as a freshman to a 27–8 record, and also shared an SEC regular-season championship. After two seasons at Alabama, Williams entered the [[2003 NBA draft]] where he was selected with the 47th overall pick by the [[Utah Jazz]]. Throughout his career, he has also played for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], [[Charlotte Hornets]] and [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. In [[2009 NBA All-Star Game|2009]], Williams was selected as an [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]]. In the [[2016 NBA Finals]], he won his only NBA championship with the Cavaliers. He retired as a player in 2017.

In May 2018, Williams became an assistant coach for the [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball]] team. In May 2020, he became the head coach for the [[Alabama State Hornets basketball]] team, but stayed for just two seasons before resigning in March 2022. A few days later he was named head coach at [[Jackson State University]] in his home town, replacing [[Wayne Brent]]. On March 30, 2026, Williams was hired as an assistant coach at the [[University of Kentucky]].

==College career==
Williams attended college at the [[University of Alabama]] under [[Mark Gottfried]]. In 2002 as a freshman, he started every game at point guard. Williams averaged 10.4 points and 4.5 assists per game. His play helped lead the Crimson Tide to a 27–8 record, including a 17–0 home record, and the SEC regular-season championship. Williams and the Crimson Tide entered the [[2002 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 2 seed, where they lost to Kent State 71–58 in the second round. Williams led the team in scoring and assists, averaging 16.4 points and 3.8 assists per game for the 2003 season, which ended in a first-round loss in the [[2003 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] to Indiana. He subsequently earned third-team All-SEC.

After two seasons, Williams decided to forgo his final two years at Alabama and declare for the [[2003 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.myplainview.com/news/article/Alabama-s-Mo-Williams-Enters-NBA-Draft-9050218.php|title=Alabama's Mo Williams Enters NBA Draft|work=MyPlainview.com|date=May 7, 2003|access-date=January 7, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Utah Jazz (2003–2004)===
Williams was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the second round, 47th overall of the [[2003 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |date=June 26, 2003 |title=Tide's Mo Williams Drafted in 2nd Round By Utah Jazz |url=https://rolltide.com/news/2003/6/26/Tide_s_Mo_Williams_Drafted_in_2nd_Round_By_Utah_Jazz |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=RollTide.com}}</ref> He averaged 5 points and 1.3 assists for the Jazz in his [[rookie]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima01/gamelog/2004/|title=Mo Williams 2003–04 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 7, 2017}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2004–2008)===
[[File:MoWilliams.jpg|thumb|180px|Williams with the Bucks in April 2008]]
On August 8, 2004, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] signed Williams, who was a restricted free agent, to an offer sheet.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.heraldextra.com/sports/basketball/professional/nba/mo-williams-signs-offer-sheet-with-bucks/article_15a423cb-2929-5e7e-8970-954e67ae32c9.html|title=Mo Williams signs offer sheet with Bucks|work=HeraldExtra.com|publisher=Daily Herald|date=August 8, 2004|access-date=January 7, 2017}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> On August 21, the Jazz decided to not match the Bucks' offer.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 21, 2004 |others=Contributed by SportsTicker and The Associated Press |title=Utah has two Olympians available at point |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=1864531 |access-date=March 22, 2023 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Filling in for Bucks' injured starting point guard [[T. J. Ford]], Williams averaged 10.2 points and 6.1 assists during the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]]. In his new role coming off the bench for the up-and-coming Bucks team, he showed a knack for clutch plays, making several game-winning shots in the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]].<ref>{{cite web |date=November 13, 2005 |title=Bucks rally, paralyze Pacers with buzzer-beater |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/games/2005-11-13-pacers-bucks_x.htm |access-date=November 13, 2005 |work=USAToday.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Borzi |first=Pat |date=January 29, 2006 |title=Clock Expires as Comeback by Knicks Falls Short |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/01/29/sports/basketball/29knicks.html |access-date=January 29, 2006 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

In the 2006 off-season, the Bucks traded Ford to the [[Toronto Raptors]] for [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] [[Charlie Villanueva]]. This opened up a position in the starting lineup for Williams. In the first 19 games of the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], Williams averaged 15.6 points, 5.1 rebounds and 6.2 assists in nearly 35 minutes per game, all career highs.

In a December 20, 2006, Bucks game vs. the [[Miami Heat]], Williams recorded his first career [[triple-double]] with 19 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=261220015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170108191338/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=261220015|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 8, 2017|title=Mo effort: Williams' triple-double helps Bucks rout Heat|work=ESPN.com|date=December 20, 2006|access-date=December 20, 2006}}</ref> On January 27, 2007, Williams scored 30 points, including making a game-winning shot, and recorded 10 assists during a 107–105 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20231204025635/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/270128015 Williams leads five Bucks in double figures in win]</ref>

Williams was a free agent in summer 2007, but decided to stay with the Bucks by signing a six-year, $52 million deal.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 16, 2007 |others=Contributed by The Associated Press |title=Williams' six-year deal reportedly worth $52 million |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2936550 |access-date=January 7, 2017 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Milwaukee Bucks |date=May 29, 2012 |title=Mo Williams Press Conference July 24, 2007 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H126W3bKRo8 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/H126W3bKRo8 |archive-date=2021-12-21 |access-date=August 8, 2013 |work=YouTube.com}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2008–2011)===
[[File:Mo Williams Cavs.jpg|thumb|left|Williams with the Cavaliers in April 2009]]
[[File:John Wall defended by Mo Williams.jpg|thumb|right|Williams with the Cavaliers in November 2010, defending [[John Wall]]]]
On August 13, 2008, Williams was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in a three-team, six-player deal involving the Cavaliers, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] that also sent Cleveland's [[Joe Smith (basketball)|Joe Smith]] and Milwaukee's [[Desmond Mason]] to Oklahoma City and sent Cleveland's [[Damon Jones]] and Oklahoma City's [[Luke Ridnour]] and [[Adrian Griffin]] to Milwaukee.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 13, 2008 |title=Cavaliers Acquire Williams in Three-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/williams_acquired_080813.html |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> Upon his arrival, he changed his jersey number to #2 because his traditional #25 was already retired by former Cavalier [[Mark Price]].

On February 10, 2009, Williams was chosen to replace forward [[Chris Bosh]] in the [[2009 NBA All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web |date=February 11, 2009 |title=Cavs' Williams gets spot after all |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/allstar2009/news/story?id=3897494 |access-date=March 22, 2023 |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> He was the second alternate choice, after [[Ray Allen]], who replaced an injured [[Jameer Nelson]]. On February 11, Williams scored a then-career-high 44 points to go along with 7 assists against the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290211005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170210134706/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290211005|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 10, 2017|title=Williams powers Cavs to 40th win; Suns without Nash|work=ESPN.com|date=February 12, 2009|access-date=January 7, 2017}}</ref>

During the 2008–09 season, Williams helped the Cavaliers reach a league-leading 66–16 record. The team went 39–2 at the [[Quicken Loans Arena]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/CLE/2009.html|title=2008–09 Cleveland Cavaliers Roster and Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 7, 2017}}</ref>

After the departure of [[LeBron James]], Williams became a very vocal member of the Cavaliers. Amidst trade rumors, Mo hinted on his Twitter account that he didn't wish to be traded. He also criticized the events surrounding LeBron's flight from Cleveland and even shot back at insults made to the Cavaliers by [[Miami Heat]] guard [[Dwyane Wade]].

On November 24, 2010, Williams made his first buzzer beater as a Cavalier, to win the game 83–81 over his former team, the Milwaukee Bucks. It was a 15-foot shot over Brandon Jennings as time expired. He scored a total of 25 points in the game and was the team's leading scorer.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/nba/gameflash/2010/11/24/28435_recap.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101126145452/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/nba/gameflash/2010/11/24/28435_recap.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 26, 2010|title=Williams' shot at buzzer lifts Cavs|work=CNN.com|date=November 14, 2010|access-date=November 14, 2010}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2011–2012)===
[[File:Mo Williams.jpg|thumb|right|Williams as a member of the Clippers in 2011]]
On February 24, 2011, Williams was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] along with [[Jamario Moon]] in exchange for [[Baron Davis]] and a first-round pick, which ended up being the first pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]], [[Kyrie Irving]].<ref>{{cite web |date=February 24, 2011 |title=CLIPPERS ACQUIRE WILLIAMS AND MOON |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews_110224.html |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> With the Clippers, Williams was immediately inserted into the starting lineup to play both guard positions, and was able to raise his averages in points-per-game and field goal percentage.

The following season, the Clippers traded for [[Chris Paul]] and claimed [[Chauncey Billups]] off waivers, making Williams the Clippers' new sixth man. He embraced the role and finished eighth in voting for [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/10/sixth-man-release/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160527054456/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/10/sixth-man-release/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 27, 2016|title=Thunder's James Harden wins Kia Sixth Man Award|work=NBA.com|date=May 10, 2012|access-date=May 10, 2012}}</ref>

===Return to Utah Jazz (2012–2013)===
On June 29, 2012, Mo Williams was traded back to the Jazz in a 4 team deal that sent [[Lamar Odom]] to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and the [[Utah Jazz]]'s trade exception to the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. The Clippers also sent their second-round pick [[Furkan Aldemir]] to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web |date=June 29, 2012 |title=Jazz Obtains Mo Williams in Four-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/20120629-trade-williams.html |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2013–2014)===
On August 8, 2013, Williams signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/itemId/3875/Default.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130813054813/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/itemId/3875/Default.aspx|url-status=usurped|archive-date=August 13, 2013|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN GUARD MO WILLIAMS|work=IAmATrailBlazersFan.com|date=August 8, 2013|access-date=August 13, 2013}}</ref> On November 23, 2013, in a game against the Warriors, Williams was ejected along with teammate [[Wesley Matthews]] after getting involved in an altercation. He was subsequently suspended for one game. Williams injured his groin in game two of the Trail Blazers' second round play-off match-up against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Holdahl |first=Casey |date=May 9, 2014 |title=Mo Williams (Groin) Unlikely To Play In Game 3 |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/mo-williams-groin-unlikely-play-game-3 |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2014–2015)===
On July 30, 2014, Williams signed a one-year, $3.75 million contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Flood |first=Sam |date=July 30, 2014 |title=Timberwolves Sign Guard Mo Williams |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-guard-mo-williams |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=July 30, 2014 |title=Timberwolves announce signing of veteran guard Mo Williams |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/timberwolves-announce-signing-of-veteran-guard-mo-williams/ |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=FoxNews.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On January 13, 2015, Williams scored a career-high 52 points on 19-of-33 shooting, breaking the franchise single-game scoring record set by [[Kevin Love]] and [[Corey Brewer]] by one point in a 110–102 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]]. This was just the third time in Williams' career that he scored more than 40 points in a game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jim|last=Johnson|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150113/MININD/gameinfo.html|title=Mo Williams scores 52, Wolves top Pacers to end 15-game skid|work=NBA.com|date=January 13, 2015|access-date=January 13, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160123035516/http://www.nba.com/games/20150113/MININD/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 23, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He subsequently earned Western Conference Player of the Week honors for the week of January 12–18.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 19, 2015 |title=Wolves' Mo Williams Named NBA Western Conference Player of the Week for Jan. 12-18 |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/williams-named-western-conference-player-week |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2015)===
On February 10, 2015, Williams was traded, along with [[Troy Daniels]] and cash considerations, to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Gary Neal]] and a [[2019 NBA draft#Draft selections|2019 second-round draft]] pick.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rochinski |first=Matt |date=February 10, 2015 |title=Hornets Acquire Guards Mo Williams, Troy Daniels from Minnesota |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-acquire-guards-mo-williams-troy-daniels-minnesota |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> He made his debut for the Hornets on February 21 against the Oklahoma City Thunder, recording 24 points and 12 assists in a 110–103 loss.<ref>{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Reed|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150221/OKCCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Westbrook nets 33, Thunder top Hornets 110–103 minus Durant|work=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2015|access-date=February 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151106103854/http://www.nba.com/games/20150221/OKCCHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 6, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> Williams continued to play well as he was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, March 2 through Sunday, March 8. Williams, who led the Hornets to the NBA's only 4–0 record in the week, was previously named Western Conference Player of the Week on January 19 while playing for the Timberwolves, making him the first player to earn the honor in both conferences in the same season since the award was split into two conferences starting with the 2001–02 season. Over the four-game week, Williams averaged 19.5 points and 10.8 assists in 35.5 minutes played, while shooting .429 from the field (24 of 56), .375 from beyond the three-point line (9 of 24) and .913 from the free throw line (21 of 23). The only Eastern Conference player to average double figures in assists, he also posted an assist-to-turnover ratio of 4.78.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wash |first=Quinton |date=March 9, 2015 |title=Mo Williams Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/mo-williams-named-eastern-conference-player-week |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Return to Cleveland (2015–2017)===
On July 10, 2015, Williams signed a two-year, $4.3 million contract with the Cleveland Cavaliers, returning to the franchise for a second stint and reuniting him with [[LeBron James]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Nick |date=July 10, 2015 |title=Cavs Sign guard Mo Williams |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/williams-signing-150710 |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Windhorst |first=Brian |author-link=Brian Windhorst |date=July 6, 2015 |title=Mo Williams returning to Cavaliers on 2-year, $4.3 million deal, sources say |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13212088 |access-date=March 22, 2023 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> In his first game for the Cavaliers since 2011, Williams recorded 19 points and 7 assists, filling in for the injured [[Kyrie Irving]] as a starter in the team's season-opening loss to the Chicago Bulls on October 27.<ref>{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Seligman|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151027/CLECHI/gameinfo.html|title=With Obama watching, Bulls hold off Cavaliers 97–95|work=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2015|access-date=October 27, 2015}}</ref> Over the Cavaliers' first 23 games of the season, Williams played in 20 of them and started in 14. Over that stretch, he averaged 13.0 points and 4.1 assists in 27.6 minutes per game, as he shared the point guard role with [[Matthew Dellavedova]]. However, upon the return of Kyrie Irving from injury on December 20, Williams' role decreased and his minutes were drastically reduced,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima01/gamelog/2016/|title=Mo Williams 2015–16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 8, 2016}}</ref> partially due to suffering from his own injury, a torn ligament in his right thumb.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Haynes|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2016/01/mo_williams.html|title=The demotion of Cleveland Cavaliers guard Mo Williams and his thumb injury status|work=Cleveland.com|date=January 10, 2016|access-date=January 11, 2016}}</ref> On January 12, he was excused by the team from their game in Dallas to tend to a personal matter.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 12, 2016 |title=Cavs guard Mo Williams excused by team from game at Mavs |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2016/01/13/ap-bkn-cavaliers-mo-williams-out |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=SI.com}}</ref> He started seeing more minutes in early February, but following the All-Star break, he appeared in just one game between February 18 and March 24 due to swelling in his left knee after being diagnosed with [[Chondromalacia patellae|chondromalacia]]. He made his return to the lineup on March 26 against the New York Knicks, scoring eight points in 13 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 26, 2016 |title=Cavaliers @ Knicks box score |url=https://www.nba.com/game/cle-vs-nyk-0021501086/box-score |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> However, in early April, he began experiencing discomfort and increased soreness in his left knee, forcing him to miss more time.<ref>{{cite web|first=Dave|last=McMenamin|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/15183207|title=Cavs guard Iman Shumpert out for final 2 games|work=ESPN.com|date=April 11, 2016|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Fendor|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2016/04/iman_shumpert_will_miss_the_re.html|title=Iman Shumpert will miss remainder of the regular season after having left knee drained; Mo Williams to visit Dr. James Andrews|work=Cleveland.com|date=April 11, 2016|access-date=April 11, 2016}}</ref> Williams received limited playing time during the Cavaliers' playoff run, a run that saw the team reach the [[2016 NBA Finals]] with a 12–2 record. Williams made his first appearance in the NBA Finals during a game 1 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Despite the Cavaliers going down 3–1 in the series following a game 4 loss, they went on to win the series in seven games to become the first team in NBA history to win the championship after being down 3–1.

On June 14, 2016, before the end of the 2016 NBA Finals, Williams exercised his player option with the Cavaliers for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Haynes|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2016/06/sources_cavs_guard_mo_williams.html|title=Sources: Cavs guard Mo Williams to pick up player option for next season|work=Cleveland.com|date=June 14, 2016|access-date=July 3, 2016}}</ref> Williams originally declared that the 2016–17 season would be his last,<ref>{{cite web|first=James|last=Herbert|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/mo-williams-announces-hell-return-to-cavaliers-for-final-season/|title=Mo Williams announces he'll return to Cavaliers for final season|work=CBSSports.com|date=September 21, 2016|access-date=September 21, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Vardon|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2016/09/mo_williams_says_hes_returning.html|title=Mo Williams says he's returning to the Cavs for 'one more year'|work=Cleveland.com|date=September 21, 2016|access-date=September 21, 2016}}</ref> but on September 26, 2016, he announced his intentions to retire from the NBA.<ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Vardon|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2016/09/mo_williams_changed_his_mind_a.html|title=Mo Williams changed his mind again and is retiring from the Cavaliers|work=Cleveland.com|date=September 26, 2016|access-date=September 26, 2016}}</ref> However, he never officially signed retirement papers and instead remained on the Cavaliers' roster.<ref name="Albertie">{{cite web|first=Quenton|last=Albertie|url=http://kingjamesgospel.com/2016/12/15/mo-williams-play-after-trade/|title=Would Mo Williams Play For Another Team|work=KingJamesGospel.com|publisher=Fansided|date=December 15, 2016|access-date=January 7, 2017}}</ref> Not being a rotation player in 2015–16 for the first time had been the most challenging time of Williams' career, and while the departure of [[Matthew Dellavedova]] in the 2016 off-season opened a spot at point guard, the Cavaliers drafted [[Kay Felder]] in the [[2016 NBA draft|2016 draft]], which would have left Williams a third-string point guard for a second straight season.<ref name="Albertie"/> Williams did not join the playing group for the 2016–17 season and in October 2016, he underwent surgery on his left knee.<ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Vardon|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2016/10/mo_williams_still_on_cavs_rost.html|title=Mo Williams, still on Cavs roster, had knee surgery Wednesday|work=Cleveland.com|date=October 12, 2016|access-date=January 7, 2017}}</ref> In January 2017, rumors began to surface of Williams being a possible trade piece for the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web|first=Josh|last=Wilson|url=http://thesixersense.com/2017/01/06/nba-rumors-philadelphia-76ers-mo-williams-season/|title=Could Mo Williams End Up on the Sixers This Season?|work=TheSixerSense.com|publisher=Fansided|date=January 6, 2017|access-date=January 7, 2017}}</ref>

Williams' final NBA game was game 7 of the 2016 NBA Finals on June 19, 2016, when Cleveland won the game (and thus the series) to the [[Golden State Warriors]] 93–89. In that game, Williams recorded 2 points, 1 turnover and 1 foul.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mo Williams 2015–16 Stats per Game – NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2178 |access-date=June 27, 2025 |website=ESPN}}</ref>

On January 7, 2017, Williams was traded, along with [[Mike Dunleavy Jr.]] and a future first-round draft pick, to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Kyle Korver]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=J. |date=January 7, 2017 |title=Hawks Acquire First round Pick, Dunleavy & Williams From Cavs For Kyle Korver |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-first-round-pick-dunleavy-williams-cavs-kyle-korver |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> He was later shipped to the [[Denver Nuggets]] alongside cash considerations on January 18, 2017, in exchange for the rights to [[Cenk Akyol]]; he was immediately waived by the Nuggets upon being acquired.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 18, 2017 |title=Denver Nuggets Trade Rights to Cenk Akyol to Atlanta Hawks |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-trade-rights-to-cenk-akyol-to-hawks-011817 |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> Two days later, he was claimed off waivers then immediately waived by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. The 76ers reportedly made the claim in order to get $2.2 million closer to the salary floor while preventing the Nuggets from doing so after Denver acquired Williams in a trade with the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 20, 2017 |title=Source: Sixers claim, then waive Mo Williams |url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/source-sixers-claim-then-waive-mo-williams/353837/ |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=nbcsportsphiladelphia.com}}</ref> He was later claimed and waived by the Nuggets on January 23 for a similar reason.<ref>{{cite web|last=Inabinett|first=Mark|url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2017/01/the_mo_williams_contract_odyss.html|title=The Mo Williams' contract odyssey continues in the NBA|work=AL.com|date=January 23, 2017|access-date=January 26, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Prada|first=Mike|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2017/1/23/14365274/mo-williams-4-different-teams-waiver-saga|title=Why Mo Williams has been on 4 different teams this year despite not playing 1 minute|work=SBNation.com|date=January 23, 2017|access-date=April 30, 2017}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
In May 2018, Williams was named an assistant coach for the [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball]] team, signalling an end to his playing career.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fenno |first=Nathan |date=May 23, 2018 |title=Former UCLA coach Jim Harrick and former NBA player Mo Williams join coaching staff at Cal State Northridge |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-csun-harrick-20180523-story.html |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> In May 2020, he was appointed head coach of the [[Alabama State Hornets basketball]] team.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 12, 2020 |title=Former NBA guard Mo Williams named Alabama State head coach |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29166761 |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> He resigned two years later on March 9, 2022.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wsfa.com/2022/03/09/mo-williams-resigns-alabama-state-mens-basketball-coach-after-2-seasons/|title=Mo Williams resigns as Alabama State men's basketball coach after 2 seasons|publisher=[[WSFA]]|date=March 9, 2022|access-date=March 11, 2022}}</ref> On March 14, Williams was named head coach at his hometown university, [[Jackson State Tigers basketball|Jackson State]], replacing [[Wayne Brent]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Gallant |first=Jacob |title=Jackson State introduces Mo Williams as head basketball coach |url=https://www.wlbt.com/2022/03/14/live-jackson-state-introduces-mo-williams-head-basketball-coach/ |access-date=March 14, 2022 |work=WLBT |date=March 14, 2022}}</ref>
